lines.text: What would actually happen to your body if you fell into a cosmic supermassive black hole?
As you drift toward the event horizon, extreme gravitational tidal forces begin stretching space.
The pull on your feet would be vastly stronger than the pull on your head.
Your body would be vertically stretched and horizontally compressed like a string of dough.
Astrophysicists call this gruesome cosmic phenomenon spaghettification.
To an outside observer, you would appear to slow down and freeze at the event horizon forever.
Crossing the threshold of a black hole is a one-way trip beyond the edge of physics itself.
